sections.label: Bill amends three Acts
sections.summary: The Bill's key amendments relate to the Companies Act 1967, the Limited Liability Partnerships Act 2005 and the Accountants Act 2004.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Bill’s key amendments relate to the following Acts: the Companies Act 1967; the Limited Liability Partnerships Act 2005 (LLP Act 2005); and the Accountants Act 2004.

sections.label: Grounds for refusing restoration
sections.summary: Clauses 84, 86, 93, 117 and 119 expressly specify grounds for refusing restoration of struck-off entities in the Companies Act 1967 and LLP Act 2005.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: While struck-off entities with the aforementioned risks are typically not restored, clauses 84, 86, 93, 117 and 119 of the Bill now expressly specify grounds for such refusal in the Companies Act 1967 and LLP Act 2005 for avoidance of doubt.

sections.label: Selective off-market purchase approval
sections.summary: Clause 50 introduces a two-tier approval process for selective off-market purchases to better safeguard shareholders' interests.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To better safeguard shareholders' interests, clause 50 of the Bill introduces a two-tier approval process for selective off-market purchases.

sections.label: Increased maximum fine and imprisonment
sections.summary: Clause 58 increases the maximum fine to $20,000, or imprisonment not exceeding 12 months, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Clause 58 of the Bill increases the maximum fine to $20,000, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months, or both.

sections.label: Audit engagement partner identification
sections.summary: Clause 32 inserts a new section 59A to the Accountants Act 2004 requiring the primarily responsible public accountant to be identified in the audit report.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To promote greater personal accountability for public accountants and transparency in the auditing profession, clause 32 of the Bill inserts a new section 59A to the Accountants Act 2004 to require the public accountant who is primarily responsible for an audit engagement to be identified in the audit report itself.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The other provisions in the Bill make technical, related and consequential amendments, including to the ACRA Act 2004, the Limited Partnerships Act 2008, the Variable Capital Companies Act 2018, Exchanges (Demutualisation and Merger) Act 1999, the Insolvency, Restructuring and Dissolution Act 2018 and the Securities and Futures Act 2001.

sections.label: Public access to electronic register
sections.summary: The Bill formalises public access to a private company's electronic Register of Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First, the Bill formalises public access to a private company's electronic Register of Members.

sections.label: Fines for administrative oversights
sections.summary: Fines for administrative oversights such as failing to update a registered office address can reach up to $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Fines for administrative oversights, such as failing to update a registered office address, can reach up to $5,000.

sections.label: Exemption criteria not yet defined
sections.summary: The Bill empowers the Minister to exempt certain classes of companies from full accounting standards, but exemption criteria have not been defined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Third, while the Bill empowers the Minister to exempt certain classes of companies from full accounting standards, the criteria for exemption have yet been defined.

sections.label: Grace period for breaches
sections.summary: As stricter penalties or shorter reporting timelines take effect, consider a six- to 12-month grace period for first-time or unintentional breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Second, as stricter penalties or shorter reporting timelines take effect, consider a six- to 12-month grace period for first-time or unintentional breaches.

sections.label: Bill aims and SME role
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to strengthen corporate governance, enhance financial transparency and align frameworks with international standards, including FATF recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: With thoughtful implementation and continued dialogue with our business community, this Bill can both enhance fairness and empower enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: They make up over 99% of all businesses, contribute nearly half of our gross domestic product (GDP) and employ about 70% of our workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But when they struggle, the ripple effects are felt across our economy and society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to strengthen corporate governance, enhance financial transparency and align our frameworks with international standards, including the Financial Action Task Force's (FATF's) recommendations on ownership disclosure and anti-laundering measures.

sections.label: Grants and adjustment period for SMEs
sections.summary: Consider targeted grants or subsidies to offset initial compliance costs and allow SMEs an adjustment period for new requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Consider targeted grants or subsidies to offset initial compliance costs, especially for digital reporting or first-time audits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Allow a reasonable adjustment period for SMEs to familiarise themselves with the new ownership disclosure and filing requirements, ensuring smooth and confident adaptation.

sections.label: Pragmatic approach to SME burdens
sections.summary: The Government should adopt a pragmatic and inclusive approach so new measures enhance transparency without imposing excessive burdens on businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Of course, we must also be mindful of the manpower and cost pressures that SMEs may face when implementing the new regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I believe the Government will adopt a pragmatic and inclusive approach to ensure that the new measures enhance transparency whilst not imposing excessive burdens on businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Through streamlining processes, strengthening training, providing financial support and phased implementation, we can help businesses transition smoothly and achieve more comprehensive results from the reforms. : Mr Speaker, the goal must be balance.

sections.label: Calibrating Bill for governance and enterprise
sections.summary: The passage states that thoughtful calibration of the Bill can achieve both robust governance and vibrant enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If we calibrate this Bill thoughtfully, we can achieve both robust governance and vibrant enterprise.

sections.label: Removal of registered office hours
sections.summary: The Bill removes the requirement for a company's registered office to be open at least three hours every business day.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In my opening speech, I mentioned that the Bill removes the requirement for a company's registered office to be open for at least three hours every business day.

sections.label: Reporting director disqualification clarified
sections.summary: The amendment clarifies that this requirement includes reporting when a director has been disqualified from acting as a director.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The amendment clarifies that this requirement includes reporting when a director has been disqualified from acting as a director.

sections.label: Grace period and six-month commencement
sections.summary: Most provisions of the Bill are targeted to commence after six months, addressing suggestions for a grace period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: On the suggestion by Mr Edward Chia and Mr Lee Hong Chuang for a grace period for companies and individuals to comply with new requirements in this Bill, most of the provisions of the Bill are only targeted to be commenced after six months.

sections.label: No expansion of data access
sections.summary: The amendments do not expand the scope of access to personal or company data.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To clarify, the amendments do not expand the scope of access to personal or company data.
